title: Education systems are facing simultaneous learning decline, socioeconomic gaps, digital distraction, and pressure to make AI use purposeful
source_unit: OECD, PISA 2025 Results (Volume I): Future-Ready Students, published 8 September 2026
geography: 15-year-old students and education systems across 91 countries and economies, with OECD and non-OECD comparisons

denominator.unit: 15-year-olds represented by the PISA 2025 assessment across 91 countries and economies, approximately

students_assessed.unit: students who took the PISA science, mathematics, and reading test in 2025, more than

countries_economies.unit: countries and economies participating in PISA 2025

oecd_performance_direction.value: lowest average levels ever observed in science, reading, and mathematics across OECD countries

assessment_endpoint.value: science, reading, mathematics, computational problem solving, engagement, school belonging, digital-device environment, and socioeconomic disparities

observations.method: OECD standardized international assessment and comparative reporting across participating education systems; this record uses the published report and aggregate tables only.
observations.uncertainty: PISA is an assessment sample and does not measure every student, classroom, school, or later-life outcome; cross-country comparisons depend on coverage, sampling, translation, and contextual conditions.
observations.subgroup: 15-year-old students, advantaged and disadvantaged students, immigrant and non-immigrant students, schools, teachers, families, and education systems.
observations.counterinterpretation: Aggregate declines coexist with systems and countries that improved; performance is shaped by curriculum, teaching, health, family resources, school climate, and assessment conditions, not a single cause.

reading_change.unit: PISA points change in average OECD reading scores from 2015 to 2025

mathematics_change.unit: PISA points change in average OECD mathematics scores from 2015 to 2025

low_performer_share.unit: percent of OECD 15-year-olds now low performers in science, mathematics, and reading, approximately one in five

hasty_reading.unit: percent of reading responses classified as fast and incorrect in 2025, nearly double the 2018 level

observations.method: OECD comparison of PISA 2015, 2018, 2022, and 2025 assessment results and performance thresholds.
observations.uncertainty: Score changes are system-level comparisons, not individual learning trajectories or causal estimates of COVID-19, technology, curriculum, or family conditions; a point change is not itself a household or labor-market outcome.
observations.subgroup: OECD students, low-performing students, reading and mathematics learners, schools, teachers, families, and education policymakers.
observations.counterinterpretation: Some systems improved and science was more stable than reading or mathematics; targeted support, teacher investment, curriculum choices, and school-level conditions can produce different trajectories.

denominator.unit: OECD PISA 2025 science-performance and school-environment comparison frame

science_advantage_gap.unit: PISA science-score difference between socioeconomically advantaged and disadvantaged students across OECD countries

science_variance_explained_by_status.unit: percent of OECD science-performance variance explained by socioeconomic status, average

school_belonging.unit: percent of OECD students who feel they belong at school

digital_distraction.unit: percent of OECD students reporting that classmates are distracted by digital devices during most or every science class

observations.method: OECD PISA 2025 comparison of science performance by socioeconomic status and reported school-environment indicators.
observations.uncertainty: Group gaps and reported school conditions do not establish causal effects of family status, belonging, or digital distraction; the narrowing of the gap since 2022 partly reflected lower performance among advantaged students.
observations.subgroup: Socioeconomically advantaged and disadvantaged students, schools, families, teachers, students experiencing digital distraction, and students with different belonging conditions.
observations.counterinterpretation: A high average belonging level can coexist with exclusion for some students, and digital tools can support learning when used purposefully; school climate and socioeconomic context vary widely across systems.

observations.period: 2025; AI and digital-tool use in learning

denominator.unit: OECD PISA 2025 students and digital-learning comparison frame

weekly_ai_chatbot_use.unit: percent of OECD students using AI chatbots weekly or more to help them learn

ai_task_performance_pattern.value: students using AI for specified schoolwork tasks such as summarising, drafting, or research scored lower in science on average than students who did not

guided_ai_pattern.value: frequent AI users who were taught to assess AI-generated information tended to perform better than frequent users without that guidance

computational_problem_solving.value: almost two-thirds reached the relevant computational-problem-solving proficiency level, but only half also demonstrated basic proficiency in science, reading, and mathematics

observations.method: OECD PISA 2025 assessment and questionnaire comparisons of AI use, digital distraction, computational problem solving, and core-subject performance.
observations.uncertainty: These are aggregate associations from an assessment publication, not causal effects of AI use; selection, prior achievement, instruction, access, and family or school context may explain part of the pattern.
observations.subgroup: Students using AI for learning, students receiving AI-evaluation guidance, teachers, schools, families, education technology providers, and policymakers.
observations.counterinterpretation: AI can support learning when used for defined purposes and with evaluation guidance; non-use is not automatically superior, and digital capability requires both tools and strong foundational knowledge.

related_sources.claim: OECD executive summary and aggregate tables for PISA 2025 performance, disparities, engagement, school climate, and digital learning.
Official OECD DOI for PISA 2025 Results Volume I.

boundary: This record adds a publication-level education-to-digital-learning route linking system performance, socioeconomic status, school belonging, digital distraction, AI guidance, and future-ready capability. It does not acquire PISA microdata, conduct respondent-level analysis, or establish causal effects on later education, work, wellbeing, or political behavior.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official OECD PISA 2025 Volume I landing page, press release, executive summary, and aggregate tables were reviewed; assessment coverage, performance changes, socioeconomic gap, school belonging, digital distraction, AI-use, and computational-problem-solving claims were cross-checked.
